name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do a weekly automated scan of all prompts using exact string matching to flag duplicates. This catches obvious duplicates reliably and is cheap to run, but misses near-duplicates and semantic duplicates—so we accept some false negatives to keep the system simple and fast. The trade-off is worth it because exact matches cover the majority of real duplicates, and we can layer a semantic scan later if needed.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching fails when prompts change slightly—like adding a comma or rewording—so it won’t catch near-duplicates, but the real risk is that it *overlooks* semantic duplicates that look different but mean the same thing, wasting effort on redundant work. A better alternative is a lightweight semantic similarity check (e.g., embeddings with a threshold) to catch near-duplicates while still being fast enough for weekly scans; settle it by running a side-by-side test on a sample of prompts to compare false negatives and runtime.
